name: South Carolina
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. South Carolina uses the last four completed quarters only if those do not qualify.
notModeled: The alternate base period: enter whichever four quarters the Department will use.
The $350 maximum is set by the Department within the statute's ceiling of two-thirds of the statewide average weekly wage; the date it took effect is not published on the pages read.

citation.sourceDocument: S.C. Code §§41-27-140, -150, -310, 41-35-40, -50; SC DEW, Weekly Benefit Amount and Claimant Handbook
citation.sourceNote: §41-27-140: the weekly average wage is the high quarter divided "by thirteen". §41-35-40(A): the weekly amount is "fifty percent of his weekly average wage", "computed to the next lower multiple of one dollar", and never "less than forty-two dollars". §41-27-310: base-period wages of "one and one-half times" the high quarter, at least "four thousand four hundred fifty-five dollars", and "one thousand ninety-two dollars" in the high quarter. §41-35-50: the total is the lesser of "twenty times his weekly benefit amount" and "one-third of his wages", rounded down to the dollar. DEW: "a minimum of $42 a week to a maximum of $350 a week". No dependent allowance; one unpaid waiting week. Read 2026-10-19.
